_doc: Construction knowledge base for the staged clothing workflow (garment_design.py, cloth_workflow.py). Data, not prose: the design sheet's defaults, the evidence checks that prove a construction choice is really in the pattern, the dimensions a tailor works to, fabrics with physical numbers, and the numeric targets a simulated garment is judged by. Lengths in mm unless a key says otherwise; ease as a fraction of the body girth (flat pattern, seam to seam). Sources: tailoring practice as summarised in cloth_audit.md (2026-10-03), the Marvelous Designer field guide 2024, Threads (shirt collars), Aldrich (skirt, trouser blocks), FreeSewing's design docs. Every lesson of the audit is either a default, an evidence check or a target here; `lessons` says which.

roles._doc: Piece roles. A piece's role is its design-table/piece key "role", else the first alias its name (without .L/.R/.m and digits) matches. Checks address roles, never piece names, so they work on any design.

kinds._doc: Garment kinds. fit: ease bands per girth (fraction of the body girth, from the flat pattern). details: the default choice per detail (garment_design fills these in when the sheet leaves them out). required: details every garment of the kind must state or take by default. cap_ease: the sleeve cap's ease into the armhole. lap: which front laps over at a closure (the buttonhole side is the outer one). sewing_order: roles in the order a maker joins them (the construction plan follows it). region: upper (shoulders carry it), lower (waist carries it), whole.

closure._doc: a dress shirt: box placket on the buttonhole side, vertical holes, French front under the buttons

wear._doc: How it is worn, by the garment / sheet key tie (default false): closure states laid over the pattern's by name (cloth.pieces via garment_design.wear). Without a tie a dress shirt's collar button AND its top front button are undone: the stand parts at the throat, the points spread, the fall lies open on the collarbones in a soft V. Closed to the top only under a tie.

no_tie._doc_spread: The open collar SPREADS (cloth._spread_open_collar, garment key collar_spread [out, down, from deg], default 18 / 14 / 65): an unbuttoned stand laid as a ring with its ends apart and carried as made stood up round the neck (su_77); worn open, in front of the neck's sides the stand and its collar swing out and tip down so the points lie toward the collarbones. At 40 / 20 / 70 it dragged the fronts' top corners apart and button 1 ended 36 mm open.
no_tie._doc_buttons: Only the COLLAR button is undone (the user on su_77, 2026-10-08: 'two buttons open when there should only be one'): every front button is closed, the first high on the chest; the V comes from the collar spreading and the fronts above button 1 rolling softly back. (Until 2026-10-08 the rule also undid the top front button and rolled the fronts to button 2.) The over front's roll ends 2 cm above button 1: run to the hole it crossed the band's inner row just above it and left one coarse triangle 3.9x stretched at the start (ZOZO: ccd failed at frame 0).
no_tie._doc_hug: An open stand still HUGS the neck at the back and sides; only its fronts part (2026-10-09). The gap is laid round the neck with the stand's length, so every cm of gap is 1.6 mm of radius: at gap 0.10 the stand stood 21-24 mm off the nape and the neck's sides, at 0.05 16 mm, and a jacket's neck point lay inside the shirt collar's wing (its forepart cleared up over it, its collar a shelf 50 mm above the shoulder). Now gap 0.03 and the opening comes mostly from the spread, 18 deg from 65 deg round. Not smaller: at 0.008 (laid as if buttoned, ends lapping 35 mm before the spread: 9-11 mm off the skin, su_garrett and su_om_garrett built, button 1 2.0 mm) ga_suit's fine construction laid the collar's end 3x stretched and the solver stopped (ccd failed); at 0.03 it builds (button 1 2.2 mm).
no_tie._doc_consistent: The stand's centre-front points must start no further apart than the fronts can follow with button 1 closed (2026-10-08, pk_31..36): the front's neck corner lies ~31 mm from its roll line, so rolled back the two corners part by about 5.3 cm x (1 - cos turn): 7-8 cm at a soft roll, 10.6 cm folded flat. Gap 0.10 + spread 25 deg started them 167 mm apart (button to buttonhole; the stand is made and ends as it starts): the fronts were held apart and button 1 ended 19 mm open with a slit of skin. Gap 0.05 + spread 12: 83 mm, button 1 3.0 mm, 0 crossings. Gap 0.02: the ends met and tangled with the collar's. And the shirt's kind is worn_top: the fronts' tops start ON the body with their neck seam pinned to the stand (start gap 95 -> 2 mm), as a front's top edge is sewn into its stand; started on the torso cylinder 10 cm away the solver hauled them up and the top button paid for it.
no_tie._doc: (older, superseded by _doc_consistent) gap:the stand's ends ~10 cm apart at the throat (an undone collar falls open by its own weight; carried as made, the stand ends as it starts; at 7 cm the V read as a narrow slit, tr_17). folds: each front rolls back above the first closed button along the line from the neck point to it, 85 deg of roll held at strength 0.5 (at 55 deg / 0.2 the sim let the fronts close again by the second button), so the V spreads to about the collarbones at the top, reaches the second button, and the collar's points lie on the collarbones. The UNDER front's roll ends 4 cm above the button: below that it lies under the over front, and rolled out to the button both flaps met at the closed button and the under one turned out through the over one (29 crossings at the start, a 2.7x stretched fine-settle start after the untangle).

collar._doc: A dress shirt collar's proportions from the wearer's neck (cloth.collar_options; tailor neckHeight = the run of the neck's sections within 8% of its narrowest girth): the stand as tall as the neck allows less a finger's room under the jaw, within the shirtmakers' 25-35 mm and never under 20 mm (a 30 mm stand on a 35 mm neck pushed 7 mm off the chin and its fall stood up); the fall at centre back 12 mm deeper than the stand, so it covers the stand's seam; points 70 mm (classic 65-75). Applied to design tables with collar_rule; a garment's own pattern options win.

lessons: Worn without a tie only the COLLAR button is undone; every front button stays closed (two open read wrong to the user). Simon's extraTopButton stays false: a button with nothing fastened to it draws as a hole on the open collar. Where: wear.no_tie (kind default).

An open collar is laid SPREAD (garment key collar_spread, default [40, 20, 70] deg): a made stand is carried as constructed, and laid as a ring it stood up round the neck to the end. Where: placement default; no check.
A buttoned collar is constructed closed and sized ~13 mm over the neck's BASE (Simon collarEase 0.115); the stand from the neck's height (see collar). Where: Simon's design table + collar_rule.

The placket must show in geometry AND maps: a box band (three layers, a crisp inner fold, two rows 3 mm in) on the buttonhole side, a French front on the button side, flat 4-hole buttons, vertical buttonholes. Where: closure finish default box / french.
STRAINED at the waist with plenty of ease was the placket's fold rows, not the fit. Read where the strain is before adding ease. Where: the fit check leaves fold rows out.
A colour sampled from a concept's lit shirt reads near white under the look's lights (#d0cbc7); a shade darker (#bdb8b4) reads as the concept. Where: none.
Tucked in = the TROUSERS worn over the shirt (trousers over: shirt); worn free the shirt hangs over the waistband and hides the belt. Where: none (the trousers' over key).

closure._doc: faced fronts (no band), horizontal buttonholes, no topstitching unless the design asks (a closure topstitch); buttons 20 mm, the cloth's colour darkened (tone x colour: horn / corozo to match), duller and thicker than a shirt's pearl (a jacket drawn with the shirt default had small white 4-hole shirt buttons); the buttonhole follows the size

lessons: Built on the form (worn_top, this kind's default): fronts and backs laid up the body over the shoulders, shoulder and CB seams pinned, the collar on that neckline, lapels pressed onto the fronts. On a cylinder the shoulder seams started 23-25 cm apart and the left lapel unrolled. Where: kind default; stage 4 start gaps.

Worn over a shirt it is DRAFTED over the shirt (over: shirt): neck = the shirt's collar size + its thickness round, armhole lowered by the shirt's thickness in the pit. From the bare body its collar climbed the shirt collar and its underarm seams stood open over the shirt. Where: automatic with over (draft log).

The tent (open fronts bowing forward to the hem) is the side panel's hem spring (contour +16 mm per edge = 64 mm of flare a side), not the chest canvas and not front balance: cut the panel seams straight below the waist. Where: none; read hem level and the open fronts on the sim.

Worn OPEN, a jacket is a loose tube hanging from chest and shoulders: its fronts hang apart and plumb, it stands off the waist all round (the concept's front-view waist is a third wider than the body). The start must say so (a front closure in state open starts the fronts apart: open_gap); started lapped, the fronts stay lapped and the ease tents in front. A stiff front (canvas bands, lapel roll strength 1) carries the upper chest's slope down to the break as a board: roll_strength ~0.3, canvas light.

Armhole depth is per body: a jacket's armhole sits ~3 cm under the pit (bodice armhole_depth 0.12-0.14; the block default 0.02 is a shirt's). Too high, the under sleeve starts through the back and side panel at the pit, the sleeves are sent down the arm and the sewing stalls the solver.
A boxy, unsuppressed body on a V-shaped torso is +25-30% at the waist: fit relaxed, not a failed regular.

Hip room comes from block_options.hips_ease (0.14 on a heavier man), never from hem flare: without it the jacket read TOO SMALL at hips, rode up 4 cm and burst its side seams. Where: stage 2 ease, partly.
front_balance (the front lengthened above the chest) was tried at 20 mm: hem level, but the raised armhole pulled the sleeves up and bunched them. Not adopted: leave 0.

Don't lower the collar stand to show more shirt collar: both lapels unrolled into a funnel (20 mm and 16 mm stands). Keep the stand (shirt stand + a few mm: 24 over a 20 mm band; 19 / fall 31 on a short neck); lower the back neck (op neckline {back} FIRST in the ops) and the notch (lapel gorge_drop ~0.12, break_y ~0.46; not yet simulated). Where: target layer_collar_show_mm measures the result.

Lapels lie on the fronts with lapel op roll_radius 0.003, roll_strength 1.0 (gap 9-11 mm; the defaults gave 12-15). made_folds on the lapels gave nothing and crossed at the gorge: leave it off. Never mark the notched collar draped (a fat roll).

Pads are support, not cloth: support [{kind: shoulder_pad, thickness: 0.012}, sleeve_head] squares the shoulders; length_bonus so the hem covers the seat; the sleeve ends 10-15 mm short of the shirt cuff.
A jacket front is not a box placket: a faced edge (closure finish facing) with buttonholes across (hole: across); worn open is closures [{name: front, state: open}].

Its pit seams (side-back, underarm) start 75-160 mm open: one start cylinder at the widest level leaves the suppressed waist's arc in one seam, and they end 40-110 mm open. Stitch stiffness made it worse. Open: read the start gaps in stage 4.

closure._doc: faced fronts (no band), horizontal buttonholes, no topstitching unless the design asks (a closure topstitch); buttons 23 mm, the cloth's colour darkened (tone x colour: horn / corozo to match), duller and thicker than a shirt's pearl (a jacket drawn with the shirt default had small white 4-hole shirt buttons); the buttonhole follows the size

lessons: Built on the form like a jacket (worn_top) and drafted over what it is worn over (over); the jacket's lessons on the tent, hip room, the stand and the lapels apply.

suit_trousers._doc: Men's tailored trousers, drafted by this kind itself (draft: the trouser block + the leg's cut per fit; each detail adds its own operation). A design sheet {kind: suit_trousers} with nothing else makes flat-front trousers with a zip fly, an extended waistband buttoned at the centre front, shaped back darts, pressed creases, belt loops and a belt, cut for a shoe.
lessons: Cut to a break: length break = 30 mm over the FLOOR, the back 12 mm longer; the start rests the hem on what faces up under it (the shoe) and gathers the extra into the bottom 9 cm. Cut from the shoe's own heights it came out 5 cm short. Give the shoes as colliders: collide [shoes, soles].
Tucked: trousers over: shirt with under_cap ~0.003; their waist is taped over the shirt (+ the layer gap) or the band lies under the shirt tail. Without the tuck no belt shows.
At the natural waist they read high-waisted: men's tailored trousers sit 4-8 cm under it (block option waist_drop).
The legs start on the legs (a tube round each leg's axis): on one cylinder a leg the front and back started as slabs 17-21 cm apart at the seams.
Shaped back darts (dart_taper 0.6): straight legs end in a poke that reads as an open tuck.
The waistband is a made band: it must start closed at its closed girth (waist ease ~2%); seams close with zozo.stitch_stiffness 8.
A shirt tucked in = these trousers over: shirt (the belt shows only then). It has passed the coarse sim, not yet the fine settle: try fine_settle false.

flat._doc: A flat thing: a tablecloth, a blanket, a curtain (state draped).

seam_finishes._doc: How a sewn seam is finished and so how it READS (cloth DETAIL seam_finish / seam_finishes; the default per garment kind is the kind's seam_finish). On real clothes a seam is a fine line: pressed open or to one side, the cloth runs across it nearly smooth; a shallow groove where the two pieces meet (0.2-0.5 mm, 1-2 mm wide), the allowances under it a faint broad rise (0.1-0.3 mm over 5-10 mm), a row or two of topstitching on some. It shows in raking light and up close; on dark wool it almost vanishes. Units m. press: the clean-up makes the surface smooth across the seam (cloth._seam_press); groove / groove_width: the line's depth and half width (Gaussian); allowance / allowance_at / allowance_width: the rise over the allowances under the cloth, its centre and half width out from the line; sides: both (pressed open: half the allowance under each side) or toward (pressed to one side: all of it under the seam's second piece, the side its rows are on); rows: topstitching rows' distances out from the line on the toward side. Lesson (2026-10-07, the user on the suits: 'ours look huge and structural'): every seam read as a welt with a valley beside it. Three causes, all fixed: pieces wound opposite ways (half the jacket's pieces faced in: welded, the shared normals cancelled into a pale or dark line, and Solidify grew the shell out on one side and in on the other), a solver stitch is a free hinge (no bending across it: the two sides met at 20-45 deg against the cloth's own 10), and the maps drew a 1.2 mm groove 5 mm wide, 0.6 mm allowance ridges 5 mm out each side, the groove 45% darker in the base colour and topstitching on every seam and hem.

pressed_open.label: plain seam pressed open (tailored jackets, trousers, skirts, coats, dresses): no stitching shows

pressed_to_side.label: plain seam pressed to one side, serged (knits, tees, linings)

topstitched.label: pressed to one side and topstitched 6 mm out (yokes, casual jackets, jeans)

edgestitched.label: pressed to one side and edge-stitched 1.5 mm out

felled.label: flat-felled (shirts' side, sleeve and armhole seams, jeans): two rows on one side, the fell a faint flat rise

welt.label: a seam made to stand: corded, piped or welted (sportswear, upholstery); not pressed

details._doc: Per detail kind, the choices. made_of: the pieces (roles) it adds, whether they're interfaced and how they rest (as_made: wholly interfaced pieces rest in their made shape; flat: rest on the flat pattern). seams: [role, role, seam kind]. folds: fold lines (see cloth_guide: angle on the pattern-face side, 180 flat, 0 folded over onto the face, 360 folded under). needs: details this choice can't be made without. dims: what a tailor works to ([lo, hi] mm unless named otherwise). evidence: checks that prove the choice is in the pattern (garment_design.EVIDENCE). lessons: why (and which audit item).

shirt_collar.label: two-piece shirt collar: a stand sewn to the neckline, a turned fall sewn to the stand's top

folds.where: 3 mm above the fall/stand seam (the roll)

lessons: The fall must cover the stand and its neckline seam by 6-10 mm at CB (audit: ours stopped 13 mm above it: a funnel). Checked: dim fall_cover on the pattern, collar_cover after the sim.
The roll is a crease a few mm above the collar/stand seam, not a 10 mm U (the U ate 15.7 mm of the fall). A fold line with angle, not a placement shape.

The stand can't be taller than the neck allows (trapezius to jaw less ~13 mm, at least 20 mm): a 30 mm stand on a 35 mm neck was pushed 7 mm off the chin and its fall stood up 15 deg; 20 mm turned 155 deg. Fall at CB = stand + 12 mm. Where: kinds.shirt.collar via collar_rule; stage 4 HINT on a band pushed > 8 mm off the neck.
Worn open, the collar is laid spread onto the collarbones (garment key collar_spread); a made stand laid as a ring stays a ring.

convertible.label: one-piece convertible collar sewn straight to the neckline (worn open or closed)

folds.where: the roll line, ~25-30 mm up at CB

notched_lapel.label: notched lapel: the fronts turn back along a roll line from the break point to the gorge, faced; a collar with stand from the gorge round the back

folds.where: the roll line: break point (top button) to the roll line's end at the neck

lessons: Interfacing stiffens the fronts but must not freeze them: fronts resting 'as made' (flat on the torso) can't roll (audit fix 1). Checked: not_made front.
Without a facing a rolled lapel shows the wrong side. Checked: piece facing.
The stand is sewn from roll-line end to roll-line end, not CF to CF (it was -23.8%).
The collar is made: marked draped it rests on the flat pattern and bends round the neck as a fat roll.

Lowering the stand unrolls the lapels into a funnel (the roll line comes down from the stand). To show more of an under collar, lower the back neck (op neckline, first) and the notch (gorge_drop, break_y).
The lapel lies on the front with the lapel op's roll_radius 0.003 / roll_strength 1.0 (gap 9-11 mm). Holding it made (made_folds) gained nothing and crossed at the gorge.

The roll line is not parallel to the neck edge: from stand_height at CB down to where the lapel's roll line crosses the neckline; past that the collar lies in the turned lapel's plane, sewn to the gorge (op collar type tailored does it).

shawl.label: shawl collar: the lapel and collar one piece cut on with the front, rolled

hood.label: hood: two sides (or sides + centre panel) sewn round the neckline, the face edge turned or bound

folds.where: the face edge turned in 20-30 mm

rib_neckband.label: rib neckband: a folded rib strip 10-15% shorter than the neckline, stretched on

folds.where: along its middle (folded in half lengthwise)

lessons: A rib band is shorter than the edge it is sewn to: that stretch is what makes it lie flat. A 1:1 band gapes.

bound_neckline.label: bias binding round the neckline (5-8 mm finished)

faced_neckline.label: neckline finished with a facing turned inside (no collar)

none.label: no collar (a raw or hemmed edge)

barrel.label: barrel cuff: a closed band buttoned round the wrist; the sleeve enters through a placket opening, 2-3 pleats folded toward it
lessons: Closed girth = wrist + 25-40 mm; height 60-70 mm (ours 57).
A closed sleeve tube sewn round a cuff whose ends overlap has nowhere to put the overlap: the sleeve needs a placket opening (audit fix 6). Checked through needs: sleeve_placket.

french.label: French cuff: a double-height cuff folded back on itself, closed with links

rib.label: knit rib cuff: a folded rib tube 15-25% smaller than the sleeve end

hemmed.label: no cuff: the sleeve end turned up and stitched

elastic.label: elastic casing at the sleeve end

tower.label: tower placket: a slit 120-150 mm on the little-finger side, an underlap binding and a pointed overlap placket
lessons: Simon drafts the sleevePlacketUnderlap/Overlap and a placketCut line; our design table didn't use them (audit fix 6).

continuous.label: continuous bound placket (a strip binding the slit)

slit.label: bound slit: the sleeve cut open 120-150 mm on the little-finger side (pattern op slit), its edges left as a narrow binding; the cuff's seam starts and ends at it, so the cuff's ends can lap. No placket strips
lessons: With the slit the cuff opens where a cuff opens (the little-finger side), not under the arm, and the sleeve tube no longer has to stretch round the cuff's lap.

none.label: no placket (sleeve end open or knit)

buttons.label: single-breasted, buttoned through a placket
lessons: The buttonhole side laps over (men's: left over right). Checked: lap.

Shirt buttons are flat 4-hole sew-through discs ~11 mm, ~2 mm thick, matte (closure key button: holes, roughness 0.42): a dome on a rim read as a rivet. Holes run along a placket (vertical) and along a cuff or stand (closures.hole_axis). FreeSewing Simon's extraTopButton adds a button 4 cm under the neck that no closure counts: off in our table.

double_breasted.label: double-breasted: two columns of buttons, the fronts overlapping 90-120 mm

single_button.label: one button at the break point (a shawl or one-button jacket), the fronts lapped by the button stand

button_stand.label: a tailored jacket or coat front: two or three buttons on the button stand below the lapel's break point; no placket (the facing is the stand's inside layer)
lessons: The top button sits at the break point (about the waist line on a two-button jacket); the lapel rolls to it, not past it.

Not a box placket: the edge is faced (closure finish facing) and the buttonholes run across (hole across); without that the shirt's placket look is drawn on a jacket. A jacket worn open keeps its buttons as a closure in state open (counted as the stand's buttons).

wrap_tie.label: wrap front: one front laps right across the other and is tied or tacked at the side

zip.label: zip front (a separating zip between the fronts)

pullover.label: no front opening (pulled over the head)

folded.label: cut-on placket: the front edge folded under twice (button side) / folded to the outside 32-38 mm (buttonhole side), interfaced
lessons: The turn op cuts the placket's folds off (one layer + an interfacing band, so the sim has no folded layers to tangle): the folds that SHOW are construction look, not cloth (closure finish: maps, a band row split into the mesh after the sim, the band pressed flat and lifted).

The pattern being right isn't enough: the band has to show. A closure's finish draws it (box: three layers proud, a crisp inner fold with the tuck's shadow, two rows 3 mm in; french: a rounded fold, no rows) and puts its edge in the mesh; a 0.8 mm lift over one 1 cm triangle was invisible. Where: closure finish default box over / french under.

separate.label: separate placket strip sewn to the front edge

half.label: half placket (polo): a short opening at CF

straight.label: straight waistband: a folded, interfaced band, 30-40 mm finished, its ends lapped and buttoned

extended.label: straight waistband opening at the CENTRE FRONT over the fly: 35-40 mm finished, interfaced, the left end laps over, the right end runs on 35-45 mm under it as an extension with the button (men's trousers)

contoured.label: contoured (curved) waistband sitting below the waist

zip_fly.label: zip fly: the centre front seam is an opening from the waist down 160-200 mm, closed by a zip under the left front's lap (a closure, kind zip: sewn when worn closed), a J of topstitching on the left front, the seam below it sewn to the fork. The fly facing and shield are not cut as pieces (they never show); the J is in the detail maps

cb_zip.label: centre-back zip 180-220 mm from the waist; the CB seam below it sewn

side_zip.label: zip in the left side seam

welt.label: welt pocket (a slot with a welt, bag inside)

in_seam.label: pocket bag in the side seam (invisible from outside)

kangaroo.label: kangaroo pocket on a hoodie's front

hem._doc: Hems aren't in the seam-line pattern: the hem depth goes to the detail maps (cloth DETAIL hem), and a fold line where the solver can hold it.

shirttail.label: curved shirttail hem, narrow double-turned 5-6 mm, edge-stitched

blind.label: blind-stitched hem 30-50 mm (skirts, trousers), invisible from outside

coat.label: coat hem 40-50 mm turned and blind-stitched (sleeve hems 30-40)

coverstitch.label: knit hem turned 20-25 mm and coverstitched (two parallel rows)

rib_band.label: rib band at the hem (hoodies, sweatshirts)

waist.label: waist darts (skirts, trousers' back): 80-140 mm long, 15-30 mm intake

box_back.label: box pleat at the back below the yoke

lapped_vent.label: lapped vent / pleat at CB: one side's extension (35-50 mm) laps over the other, tacked at the top, NOT sewn full length
lessons: Carlton's tail CB was sewn shut full length: the 36 mm strips lay in the plane (the 'crossings at the vent'). Audit fix 5.

back_belt.label: a half belt between back and tail (Carlton): it closes the gap the side seams need
lessons: Leaving Carlton's belt out made back + tail 83 mm shorter than the front side seam (-20.5% / -5.6%).

leather.label: a leather belt through the loops, 30-35 mm, buckled at the centre front: a TRIM (cloth_trims.py), built on the finished waistband, not simulated

loops.label: belt loops: 7 on men's trousers (centre back, two on the back, two behind the side seams, two at the front creases), 10 mm wide, standing a belt's thickness off the band: a TRIM built on the finished waistband

pressed.label: a pressed crease front and back down the grain line (through the middle of knee and hem): the front's from the hem to the waistband, the back's to the seat. A press fold standing out (205 deg), strength 0.6
lessons: Without a crease a suit trouser reads as a pyjama leg whatever its cut: the crease is what makes the leg hang as two planes.
The crease is also pressed into the geometry after the sim and drawn as a ridge in the maps; the sim's own turn across it is soft (8-36 deg).

pad_and_head.label: shoulder pad + sleeve head roll
lessons: Pads are not cloth: garment key support [{"kind": "shoulder_pad", "thickness": 0.012}, "sleeve_head"] (pads on the body under the garment). Without them a jacket's shoulders slope soft; they add tension at the pit seams.

edge.label: edge-stitched 1.5-3 mm from collar, stand, cuffs, placket edges

flat_fell.label: flat-felled seams: two rows 6 mm apart on one side

interfacing._doc: Bending multiplier over the shell per stiffening (cloth FABRICS 'stiff' is the solver's multiplier; real fused interfacing is 5-20x the shell's bending).

fabrics._doc: Fabric choices with physical numbers (weight g/m2, thickness mm, stretch: woven or knit, bending length mm = (B/w)^(1/3), the drape scale) and the cloth preset + overrides the solver gets. A 'fabric' in a design sheet is one of these names, or a cloth preset name, or {preset, overrides}.

designs._doc: What each draft source can make: per detail choice, the recipe (FreeSewing options, pieces dropped, fold lines, generated pieces) and what it can't make yet (and why). A sheet choice a design can't make is a hard failure in stage 1. fit_options: draft options per fit. pattern_from: the cloth design table / block name (default: the design's own name).

cannot.sleeve_placket.tower: the table cuts the placket slit and sews the cuff from it (choose "slit"), but the underlap and overlap strips Simon drafts aren't sewn on yet
cannot.sleeve_placket.continuous: the slit is cut (choose "slit"); no binding strip piece yet
cannot.placket.separate: separateButtonPlacket isn't in the design table

cannot.lining.full: the table is the shell only (no lining pieces)
cannot.lining.half: the table is the shell only

draft._doc: block + ops (pattern_draft.py): judged by evidence in the pieces, not by a recipe table

cannot.back_vent.lapped_vent: no vent extension in the block yet

targets._doc: Numeric targets a simulated garment is judged by (cloth_audit.md part 3; measured on reference photos). stage: which quality they apply to ('final' = at <= 5-10 mm triangles; 'draft' numbers are reported, not judged). The workflow's sim check reads these.

seam_gap_p95_mm._doc: sewn vertex pairs after the clean-up: a seam left open shows as a pale line down the garment

closure_gap_max_mm._doc: the widest a button / zip / tie stitch stands open: a closure must close its opening

collar_cover_mm._doc: how far the fall's edge lies below the neckline seam at CB (+ = covers)

layer_collar_show_mm._doc: layered (cloth_layers.tells): the under garment's collar above the outer collar at CB (a shirt collar over a jacket's)

layer_cuff_show_mm._doc: layered: the under cuff past the outer sleeve's hem, along the forearm

layer_lapel_gap_mm._doc: layered or not: a lapel's flap off the front it lies on

layer_collar_hug_mm._doc: layered: the outer collar and stand off the under collar's surface (median)

layer_crossings._doc: layered: edges of either garment through the other's triangles

hem_level_mm._doc: hem height spread across the front (hung: hem swing) or round the body (a skirt worn)

waistband_at_waist_mm._doc: waistband's median height minus the body's waist line

crest_radius_p10_mm._doc: needs <= 5 mm triangles; at 1 cm the floor is ~7 mm

crease_width_mm._doc: FWHM from renders (audit method); not measured by the tools yet

fold_spacing_mm._doc: not measured by the tools yet

start_strain_over_limit._doc: strain-limited solvers (ZOZO) can't start past their limit: triangles of the start stretched past it against the rest

lessons.lesson: Construction before solver: a day of stiffness/shear/mesh tuning chased symptoms whose cause was the pattern (cap ease 44%, a stretched stand, a missing belt, a pleat sewn shut, no sleeve placket, no lapel roll or facing, nothing pressed, one bend for every fabric).
lessons.where: workflow: dress refuses to simulate while design/pattern checks fail hard (force=True overrides)

lessons.lesson: Sleeve cap ease: shirt 0-3%, coat/jacket 3-6%, knit -3..+3%.
Every seam within +-1.5% unless it is designed to ease; notches aligned within 6 mm.
A notched lapel needs a roll line (fold), a facing and fronts that aren't frozen as made.
A barrel cuff needs a sleeve placket.
The collar fall covers the stand by 6-10 mm at CB.
Layers lie touching (1 mm shirt, 3-4 mm coat): placement offsets of 4-10 mm read padded.
The cloth reads thick below ~7 mm crests at 1 cm triangles: finals at <= 5 mm on visible pieces.
Every fabric its own bend: fabrics carry physical numbers, interfacing its multiplier.
Hems differ by kind: shirttail 6 mm, blind 40 mm, coat 45 mm, none on bagged collar/cuff edges.
Coat buttons are 20-25 mm, shirt 10-12 mm; buttonholes horizontal on cuffs, stands and coats.
lessons.where: details.front_closure dims (maps don't size buttons per design yet)

lessons.lesson: A strain-limited solver can't start past its limit; nothing may start through anything else.
Interfaced pieces resting as made keep their placed shape: fine for a collar or cuff, wrong for anything that must roll (coat fronts).
Sleeves on a hanger hang within ~8 deg of vertical.

Fix the START, not the solver: a seam that starts far apart closes badly or not at all, and stiffer stitches don't help (a jacket's pit seams got worse at stitch stiffness 3). Read the start's seam gaps.
lessons.where: place stage: seam start gaps (no failure on distance alone)

lessons.lesson: Start stretch is shear too: edges within 5% can be 9-12% stretched along the diagonal. A strain-limited solver needs every start triangle near its limit (3%).
lessons.where: place stage start strain; the fine settle's start check (1.6x) refuses before the GPU

lessons.lesson: A garment worn over another is drafted over it (neck = the under collar + its thickness, armhole lowered by the under layer in the pit), placed on it pressed (under_cap), and judged by layer tells.
Jackets and coats are built on the form (worn_top): fronts and backs laid up the body over the shoulder, not on a cylinder.
A made band closed on itself (cuff, collar stand, waistband) must start closed at its closed girth: it is held as made.
lessons.where: place stage: band starts open fails

lessons.lesson: A padded body (the body pushed out by an under garment) folds round hollows deeper than they are wide (the neck under an open collar, the armpit); clearances read the fold backwards.
Judge surfaces in clay or the exported GLB, not the textured EEVEE look (shards). A render made before a code change or merge shows the old code; sims before a cache-key change need a re-sim.
Body measurements moved on 2026-10-06 (taut tapes, shoulder line slope): drafts before then aren't comparable.

principles._doc: How a garment that doesn't exist yet is designed: a block (a basic pattern drafted from the body by rule) + pattern-making operations (pattern_draft.py) + details. Flat pattern making as Aldrich, Armstrong and Mueller & Sohn teach it; FreeSewing's own designs are derived the same way (Simon and Teagan from the Brian block, Carlton and Jaeger from Bent = Brian with a two-piece sleeve, trousers from Titan). Ready-made drafts are references to check ours against, not the capability.
three_principles: Dart manipulation: the shaping a body needs (a dart's angle) can be moved anywhere round its apex without changing the fit: to another edge, into a seam (princess), into ease, gathers, pleats or flare.
Added fullness: slash and spread (or close) to add (or take out) cloth where the design wants it; the hinge edge keeps its length.
Contouring: cloth lying closer than the block does over a hollow (under the bust, the waist, a cut-away armhole or neckline) has the excess taken out along a seam or edge.

bodice.from: neck, shoulder width and slope, chest, waist, hips, hps-to-waist, waist-to-armpit, hps-to-bust
rules: neck width = neck (1 + ease) / 4.8; back neck depth 5% of the neck; the front neck depth is SOLVED so back + front neckline = half the neck girth + ease
shoulder point at half the shoulder width, dropped by the shoulder slope from the neck point
armhole depth = hps-to-waist - waist-to-armpit (1 - 2% - half the biceps ease)
chest quarter = chest (1 + ease) / 4, front and back alike (a full bust or round back moves the side seam)
across back 98% of the half shoulder width at the pitch, across front 93% (the front armhole is hollowed more)
waist suppression = chest quarter - waist quarter: up to 40% (at most 25 mm) at the side seam, the rest (at most 35 mm) in a waist dart or left for panel seams
a bust dart from the side seam, level with the apex, when the bust is fuller than the high bust; the front below it is longer by its intake
bodice.options: chest_ease, waist_ease, hips_ease, collar_ease, shoulder_ease, biceps_ease, armhole_depth, length (hips | waist | m), fitted, darts, bust_dart, cb / cf (fold | seam | open)

rules: the bodice with 0-2% ease (the cloth stretches), no darts, a looser neck (it must pass the head), a cap without ease

sleeve.from: biceps, shoulder-to-wrist, shoulder-to-elbow, wrist + the armhole it is sewn into
rules: width = biceps (1 + ease)
cap length = armhole length (1 + cap ease): shirt 0-3%, jacket and coat 3-6%, knit 0

the cap HEIGHT is solved from the two: a wide sleeve gets a low flat cap (shirt: more lift, drag lines when the arm hangs), a narrow sleeve a high cap (tailored: clean when hanging, less lift); the top is shifted until the front and back parts match the front and back armholes
a sleeve wider than the armhole is long can't be capped: less ease or a deeper armhole
quarters of waist and seat with ease; the difference shared between the side seam (half, at most 30 mm) and darts (the back's larger); the side waist raised 10 mm

trouser.from: waist, seat, waist-to-seat, body rise, waist-to-knee, waist-to-floor
rules: front seat quarter - 10 mm, back + 10 mm
body rise (crotch depth) from the waist: measured, or 0.175 x waist + 154 mm
fork (crotch extension) seat / 16 + 5 mm at the front, about twice that at the back (the seat needs it)
the back centre seam leans in 35 mm and rises 20 mm at the waist (the seat angle); a back dart takes the rest
a crease line midway between side seam and fork; knee and hem widths about it, the back 20 mm wider than the front
the back fork is dropped until the back inseam is 5 mm shorter: stretched onto the front it hollows the back thigh

the leg's cut from the leg itself (option leg: skinny / slim / tapered / straight / wide; pattern_blocks.LEG_CUTS): finished knee = knee girth + ease (slim 20%, straight 32%), never under calf + ease (slim 8%: the leg must hang clear of the calf); finished hem = a share of the knee (slim 88%, straight 92%), never under the heel-and-instep girth + 20 mm (what the hem must pass over). Ready-to-wear on a 36-38 cm knee: slim suit trousers knee 42-44 cm, hem 36-38 cm; classic knee 48, hem 42-44 cm (Aldrich's men's block: bottom 25 cm flat classic, 20-22 slim; Cabrera: knee 19-20 in, bottom 17-18 in)

the crease IS the grain line: plumb through the middle of the knee line and the middle of the hem on both pieces, pressed from the hem to the waistband at the front and to the seat at the back (Cabrera: 'the crease line is the straight grain')

length: the hem of a suit trouser ends on the shoe's heel seam at the back (about 30 mm over the floor) and rests on the instep at the front with one shallow break (option length: break = 30 mm over the floor at the front and sides, the back 12 mm longer, the front's length over the vamp gathered into one break as it rests on the shoe; shoe = 30 mm over the floor all round, no gathering); a slim hem takes less break than a wide one

the back dart 15-20 mm x 90-120 mm, pointing at the fullest part of the seat, its legs equal and SHAPED (running in toward the fold over the last third: option dart_taper) so the point dies away; pressed toward the centre back

men's fly: left over right, the opening 160-200 mm from the waist, ending on the straight part of the centre seam above the crotch curve; the waistband opens with it, its right end extended 35-45 mm under the left with the button

style_line.does: cuts a piece in two along a drawn line; the two new edges are the same line
style_line.use: princess seams, yokes, panels, colour blocking
style_line.keeps: sewn 1:1; with take_in both edges are shaved alike (contouring)

dart.does: moves a dart to another edge about its apex
dart.use: side dart to shoulder, neck, armhole, waist, centre front
dart.keeps: every seam length (the outline only turns)

dart_to_ease.does: closes a dart by straightening its edge
dart_to_ease.use: gathers under a yoke, ease over a shoulder blade, a soft waist
dart_to_ease.keeps: declares the intake as ease on that seam

flare.does: slash from an edge to a hinge and spread (or close)
flare.use: A-line, swing, peplum, bell sleeve, tapering
flare.keeps: the hinge edge's length; the slashed edge is trued to a curve

lengthen.use: cropped, tunic, dress and coat lengths
lengthen.keeps: mating seams when both pieces are named

extend.use: button stand (button diameter, at least 15-20 mm), wrap overlap, vent extension, cut-on facing
extend.keeps: the old edge as a line (the centre front, a fold)

reshape.does: moves a point, neighbours eased along
reshape.use: lowered or widened necklines, curved hems, a dropped shoulder

facing.does: traces a new piece from a piece along edges
facing.use: front and neck facings, hem facings, waist facings
facing.keeps: sewn 1:1 to the edge it was traced from, turned in

collar.does: drafts a collar from the neckline as it is now
collar.use: band / stand (a strip: stands up), flat (the neckline's own curve: lies flat), roll (between: the straighter the sewn edge, the higher the stand)

sleeve.does: drafts the sleeve into the armhole as it is now (after any style lines)

two_piece.does: top and under sleeve from the one-piece: seams moved under the arm
two_piece.keeps: cap length; forearm seams equal; the top's hindarm a little longer (elbow ease, declared)
two_piece.options: shift (forearm seam under the quarter line, 0.02), shift_back (hindarm), elbow (m the wrist comes forward: each piece swings below the elbow line about its forearm seam's elbow point; 0 = straight)
two_piece.why: a tailored sleeve hangs bent like the arm: the forearm seam hollows, the hindarm opens over the elbow, the hem ends square to the forearm. A jacket sleeve also wants sleeve hem_width ~0.28 (the block's default is a shirt cuff's)
two_piece.limits: the under sleeve's top is the two underarm hollows joined (symmetric), not a tailor's S curve

contour.does: shapes an edge: moved into its piece (negative: out) by an amount per level, eased between: {"edge": "centre_back", "at": [["top", 0], ["chest", 0.006], ["waist", 0.02], ["hem", 0.004]]}
contour.use: a shaped centre-back seam (block cb: seam), side seams shaped on front and back alike, a hem's spring over the seat, a style line let out below the waist (its name shapes BOTH edges)
contour.keeps: mirror seams (centre back) equal; a panel seam's small difference declared as pressed / eased on
contour.why: a straight centre back stands away from the hollow of the back; 15-25 mm out at the waist is half a tailored back's shape

join.does: two pieces sewn together become one piece, the seam gone: {"a": "side_front", "b": "side_back", "name": "side"} ("along": a point on the seam meant, when they share two)
join.use: a side panel that drops from the armhole with no side seam (cut front and back from the armhole to the hem, join the two side parts), a yoke or band cut on, front and back in one
join.keeps: every other seam and named edge (the armhole, the hem run over the joined piece); b's clashing point names become name@b
join.why: the seam's CURVE carried shaping: joined, the two edges meet only at their ends and that shaping is lost (the log says how many mm): take it in the panel seams beside it

round_corner.does: a corner of the outline rounded: {"piece": "front", "corner": "cfHem", "along": [0.09, 0.06]}
round_corner.use: a cut-away front hem, patch pocket corners, cuffs, collar points
round_corner.keeps: the corner's name (on the curve's middle), so edges named to it still run
round_corner.why: do it before a facing or band is traced from those edges

pocket.does: a pocket by type. Laid ON a piece (traced in its coordinates, on its outside face, tacked by point stitches along its sewn edges): patch (a rectangle, bottom corners cut, top open; at = [x, y] of the top edge's middle), kangaroo (across the centre front of a piece cut on the fold; top and bottom sewn, slanted sides open), welt (a 12 mm strip sewn down all round: the slot's lip), flap (hangs from its top edge). IN A SEAM: in_seam (piece = the front, other = the back, top = m below the seam's upper end, opening, width, height): the seam is left unsewn over the opening and two bags are sewn to its lips and to each other, lying inside the front
pocket.use: patch pockets on jackets, shirts, aprons; a kangaroo pocket; a tailored jacket's welt and flap pockets; side-seam pockets in skirts, trousers, dresses, coats
pocket.keeps: the piece under a laid-on pocket is unchanged; an in-seam pocket splits its seam in two, both parts still matched
pocket.limits: a welt / flap pocket's slot is not cut and has no bag (a cloth mesh has no holes; the bag never shows)

lining.does: a lining derived from its shell: every body piece traced as <piece>_lining, the seams between lined pieces repeated between their linings, each laid inside its shell, sewn to the shell along attach (default the hems, sleeve hems and back neck)
lining.use: jackets, coats, lined skirts; do it last, before unfold
lining.keeps: every lining seam matches as its shell's does
lining.limits: the same outline as the shell: no centre-back pleat, not trimmed to the facing, one fabric for shell and lining

fisheye.does: a double-pointed dart inside a piece that runs past the waist; run on to the hem as a closed cut (a cloth mesh can't hold a cut that doesn't reach an edge)
fisheye.use: fitting a hip-length block without panel seams; block option darts: true makes them on a hip-length bodice
fisheye.keeps: its two legs equal; the hem edge (in two parts either side)

neckline.does: redraws the neckline on front and back together: neck point moved along the shoulder by the same amount on both, centre front / back lowered; round, V or square
neckline.use: wide and boat necks, V necks, before a collar, facing or cut
neckline.keeps: the shoulder seams equal (both shortened alike)
neckline.why: cutting one side's neck wider leaves the other shoulder longer: the seam no longer matches

shawl.does: a shawl collar cut on with the front: button stand, break point, a roll line from it past the neck point, the collar grown on beyond the shoulder with its neck seam the back neck's length and a centre back seam
shawl.keeps: neck seam = back neck; the two collar halves' CB seam equal; a roll fold on the front
shawl.limits: the placement lays the collar up the front of the neck; sewing must bring it round (Blender's draft sim crumples it): needs a fold-aware start

lapel.does: a notched lapel: front edge extended, break point, lapel point set from the roll line, roll fold; then collar with "stop" ends the collar at the gorge
lapel.keeps: the neckline for the collar; the lapel and gorge as named edges for a facing

cut_away.does: cuts a piece along a line and discards one side; the new edge is named
cut_away.use: V necklines, cut-away fronts, cropped or slanted hems, asymmetric designs (after unfold)
cut_away.keeps: the kept side's seams (shortened where the cut crossed them: consistency then fails until the mate is shortened too: start a neck cut at the neck point, or widen both with neckline)

darts_to_seam.does: joins two darts of a piece through their tips into a panel seam: the dart legs become the seam's shaping
darts_to_seam.use: princess seams from a darted block (shoulder or armhole princess)
darts_to_seam.keeps: the suppression of both darts; the two new edges sewn to each other

raglan.does: front and back cut from the neckline to the armhole; the shoulder parts joined to the sleeve cap, the shoulder seam left as an overarm dart
raglan.keeps: armhole / cap lengths of the remaining underarm; the neckline now runs over the sleeve

kimono.does: the sleeve cut in one with the body: the shoulder line run on to the wrist, an underarm curve
kimono.limits: pattern only: no placement for a sleeve grown onto a torso piece yet

hood.does: a two-piece hood from the head's measures, its neck edge the neckline's length
hood.limits: pattern only: no head wrap in the placement yet

pleat.does: spreads a piece by twice the depth along a line that crosses it and adds the two press folds; seams skip the underlay
pleat.use: box and knife pleats, a shirt's back pleat run to the hem
pleat.limits: a pleat that dies inside the piece isn't a fold the solver takes (a fold line must cross its piece)

buttons.does: button marks down a line of a paired piece; at unfold they are a closure (left front over right, a fastening per mark) with a wear state: state closed | open (worn unbuttoned: buttons, no stitches) | {open_above: mark}; size = button diameter

stitch.does: a point stitch between two named points (a tie, a tack)

unfold.does: halves into the garment's pieces, seams mirrored
unfold.use: runs last; operations after it address whole pieces (asymmetric designs)

derivations._doc: Each garment category: which block, which operations, why. An LLM designs a new garment by writing this list for it.

shirt.block: bodice (dartless, 10-20% chest ease, to the hips)
ops: style_line: back yoke
dart_to_ease or a pleat under the yoke
extend: button stands
collar: band + roll (stand and fall)
sleeve (cap ease 0-3%, a low cap)
cuffs from the sleeve hem, a placket slit
shirt.why: ease for movement, a low cap for reach, structure only at collar, cuffs and plackets

blazer.block: bodice (fitted, 8-15% chest ease, to below the seat)
ops: dart: front waist dart, or style_line from the armhole (a side panel) with take_in
style_line: back panel or CB seam with take_in
extend: front edge for the button stand
notched lapel: a roll line from the break point (top button) to the neck, the lapel drawn on the front and mirrored over the roll line, the collar drafted on the roll line's extension
facing: the front edge and lapel
sleeve (cap ease 3-6%, a high cap) + two_piece
extend: back vent
lining = the shell's pieces with pleats for ease
blazer.why: the shaping moves into panel seams; the high cap and two-piece sleeve hang clean with the arm down; canvas and facing make the lapel roll

cropped_jacket_shawl.block: bodice (fitted, to just under the waist)
ops: style_line: princess from shoulder or armhole through the apex, take_in at the waist
lengthen: negative, to the cropped length
shawl collar: the front extended past the neck point along the roll line by the back neck length, CB seam, the facing cut in one with the upper collar
sleeve + two_piece
cropped_jacket_shawl.why: princess seams carry the bust and waist shaping with no dart showing

wrap_dress.block: bodice (fitted, darted) + skirt, or a knit block to the knee
ops: unfold first (asymmetric)
extend: each front past the centre by the wrap
reshape: the neckline to a V running into the wrap edge
dart: bust dart into the side seam or the wrap's gathers
flare: the skirt
ties sewn at the wrap's ends, an opening in one side seam
sleeve
wrap_dress.why: the overlap is the closure; the V neckline's length is on the bias and is usually stayed

ops: reshape: shoulder dropped and lengthened
sleeve into the deeper armhole (flat cap, no ease)
hood from head measures: two sides whose neck edge = the neckline, height = neck base to crown + ease, a centre seam or panel
kangaroo pocket: a patch traced on the front
rib bands at hem and cuffs at 80-90% of their edge
hoodie.why: the knit's stretch replaces darts and cap ease; bands shorter than their edges pull the hem in

ops: style_line on front and back from the neckline to the underarm
the cut-off shoulder parts are joined to the sleeve cap at the pitch points (a shoulder dart or overarm seam takes the angle)
raglan.why: the armhole seam becomes two diagonal seams; reach improves, the shoulder line softens

ops: dart: half the dart closed into flare at the hem (slash from the hem to the dart tip)
flare at the side seams, equal front and back
a_line_skirt.why: closing a dart into flare keeps the waist fit while the hem opens

ops: flare from the hem to the seat line on both seams equally
lengthen above the waist for a high rise
front pleats: slash along the crease from the waist and spread
waistband from the waist edges
wide_trousers.why: width is added equally either side of the crease so the leg still hangs on grain

rules.ease: Wearing ease (to move in) + design ease (the look). Chest, woven: fitted 5-8%, shirt 10-20%, jacket 8-15% over a shirt, coat 15-30% over a jacket; knits 0 to negative. Waist of a skirt or trousers 0-3% (it hangs there); seat 4-8%.
rules.balance: Front and back hang level from the shoulder: the front is longer than the back over a bust (the bust dart's intake) and the back longer over a round back; side seams are the same length and meet at the same levels.
rules.grain: The straight grain runs down the centre front and back, the sleeve's centre and the trouser crease, so each piece hangs plumb; collars, cuffs and waistbands lengthwise on grain (they don't stretch); bias only where drape or stretch is wanted.
rules.shaping: Shaping points at an apex (bust, shoulder blade, seat, elbow). A dart's intake is an angle; a seam through the apex can carry it invisibly. Darts stop 15-25 mm short of the apex.
rules.seams: Mating edges are the same length unless ease is intended: cap into armhole, back shoulder onto front (2-4%), back inseam onto front (5 mm). After any slash, true the edge to a smooth curve and check corners meet square at seams.
rules.proportions: Button stand = button diameter (15-20 mm shirts, 25-40 mm coats); facing 60-90 mm; hems by kind (see details.hem); collar stand 30-35 mm; princess line over the apex, 1/3 to 1/2 along the shoulder; back yoke 1/4 of the armhole depth below the neck; vent 180-250 mm.

sources: Winifred Aldrich, Metric Pattern Cutting (bodice, sleeve, skirt and trouser blocks; ease in the bodice: https://dresspatternmaking.com/patternmaking-basics/analyzing-other-block-making-intro/ease-in-the-bodice-aldrich)

Helen Joseph-Armstrong, Patternmaking for Fashion Design: the three principles (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/patternmaking-principles1pptx/253196411; dart manipulation: https://www.thecreativecurator.com/dart-manipulation-types-of-darts/)
M. Mueller & Sohn: lapel and shawl collars drafted on the break line (https://www.muellerundsohn.com/en/?p=2391)

FreeSewing's blocks (Brian after Gareth Kershaw; Bent = Brian with a two-piece sleeve; Titan for trousers): https://freesewing.org/docs/designs/brian ; https://freesewing.eu/docs/designs/bent/ ; https://freesewing.org/docs/designs/titan
